analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the last-updated date and adds a command-table row (head line 156) plus a new `darkbloom addon` section (head lines 905-932) describing operator debugging of add-on holds (status/hold/release). No source or control code is changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no regression to the T-041 prefix-cache posture, the logout/revocation lifecycle (T-053/A-008), or the attestation/authorization boundaries (TB-011).

Security-relevant claims in the new section: commands reach the running provider through an owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to live process identity; add-ons use a separate local socket; `hold` closes admission, finishes accepted work for up to 120 s, then unloads every model; `release --force` bypasses the machine-lock refusal. The hold lease is documented as 30-600 s. Availability impact is limited to the local operator or add-on that can reach the mailbox/socket. The implementation (AddonCommand.swift, ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift, the addon-hold IPC reference) is not supplied. Whether the owner-only mailbox and the add-on socket enforce peer authentication, and whether a local unprivileged process can place or renew a hold (a DoS on serving, TB-003 / T-010-class availability), cannot be verified from this doc diff. The threat model has no explicit entry for the add-on hold surface. A source-bearing pass should check that and whether TB-003 or a new threat needs to cover it.

The remaining unchanged parts of the file (logout, drain, prefix-cache, App Attest text) were read as context. Their statements agree with the canonical model: logout confirms remote revocation only on HTTP 204, and App Attest coverage is unchanged. I identified no contradictions.
